# v0.17.7 payload evidence fixture

This directory contains public metadata and source comparison inputs. It contains no installed-payload identity, reviewed production policy, signer private key, or installer binary. A passing fixture does not admit an installer into production.

## Exact scope

The `Historical payload evidence` workflow is restricted to same-repository PRs from `feat/unified-workspace-ux` into `feat/native-cli-finalization` that change the dedicated fixture/workflow/provenance paths. It checks out and verifies the event’s exact head SHA. Optional later manual dispatch requires a reviewed 40-character source SHA. Other existing workflows can still run on that push; they use separate VMs and do not execute these ignored installer entrypoints. The `clean` and `seeded-existing` matrix entries run on separate disposable Windows 2022 VMs. No runner cache/profile is reused and no ordinary Rust test or application startup precedes the initial absence check. Build preparation and compilation happen first. Do not run the ignored entrypoints on a user's computer or general-purpose development VM.

The test controller creates only a temporary same-user restricted token with `LUA_TOKEN | DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE`. It records the parent and candidate token. The gate requires the same SID/session, false elevation, medium integrity, no enabled administrator SID, and no privilege other than change-notify. An unsupported token stops before profile seeding or installer execution. The controller then creates only the exact worker test, suspended, checks its actual token, puts that fixture worker in a kill-on-close job, records its exact process identity, and resumes once. It never changes UAC, accounts, passwords, token integrity labels or security policies, and never uses `SANDBOX_INERT`. These are test-only helpers; production does not manipulate tokens.

The worker repeats the token check, positively checks absent Desk data/install locations, six registration slots in both registry views and hives, relevant shortcuts, matching machine/WiX registration, and matching running Desk processes. Process-name observation is a fixture refusal check, not production quiescence authority. It requires both existing WebView registration and a successful WebView loader version lookup, without starting a browser or downloading a prerequisite.

The worker uses the production official catalog, bounded asset transport, preparation service and committed Minisign key. It pins release 392398817, installer 576637999 (4,966,193 bytes, SHA256 `e9ffbc5ba627f0c133a4385db404342a7344729339185e6f9b8ee6b5969086ac`) and signature 576637991 (420 bytes, SHA256 `30b26f21c76d8c30bf4ca042ff699f1dd5d181af54f0e8956a3bff10650b80e2`). Selected asset IDs, names, sizes, digests, URLs, creation/update times, and release identity/timestamps must match the committed tuple. It retains the original verified package and copies exact verified bytes into a create-new executable; a no-write/no-delete pinned file handle stays held through process consumption.

Only production `CommandLine::nsis` and `PreparedProcess` execute the installer: explicit application, `/S /UPDATE /NS`, final unquoted `/D=` path containing spaces and Chinese characters, no `/R`, a private installer job, durable launch/identity/resume records, actual installer token verification, bounded terminal wait and observed empty job. No historical app or uninstaller is explicitly launched. Failures are not retried and fixture state is not cleaned up by guessing.

The seeded case creates only fresh fixture-owned old registration, old-target shortcuts, a never-executed `Old Desk.exe` placeholder, and a source-only leftover. It measures old-binary deletion, `/NS` shortcut migration, `/UPDATE` leftover retention, overwriting CC Desk Explorer values and deletion of both legacy cc-box Explorer trees. The clean case alone cannot establish these behaviors.

## Evidence and limits

Artifacts retain token/environment/process/command receipts, the exact official installer and signature, raw typed registry/security snapshots, raw known shortcuts, installed PE identity and a complete bounded installed-tree inventory with file identities, attributes, owner/DACL descriptors, sizes and SHA256. Raw installed files are copied into the artifact area only after a complete regular-file inventory and a second held-object/digest comparison. Upload paths exclude the live install and package-store trees, so unsupported/reparse objects are not recursively uploaded. Evidence remains available after failure wherever capture was possible.

Budgets are explicit: 120-second installer wait, 300-second worker wait, 256 tree entries/16 levels, 256 MiB per file/512 MiB total payload, 4 MiB per report, 64 registry nodes across a phase, 32 values/subkeys per node, 4 KiB per registry value, 64 KiB per descriptor or shortcut, 4,096 machine uninstall keys and 16,384 process entries. Inventory overflow and unsupported objects are blockers, not truncation success.

Source comparison inputs pin the v0.17.7 config/hooks/resources and the Tauri 2.10.1 NSIS template. The defaults are documented upstream at `https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-cli-v2.10.1/crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs`. Those sources do not independently attest that arbitrary signed bytes were compiled with that exact contract. The fixture does not claim a whole-system effect trace, deterministic generated uninstaller bytes, correct data switching, rollback, shared-current-data compatibility, or a successful real return. Independent review must compare the clean and seeded outputs and decide whether a narrowly keyed policy is justified. Unknowns remain blockers to that later admission.

Local checks: `node --test tests/scripts/historyPayloadFixture.node.mjs`; Windows test registration and `Win32_UI_Shell`, `Win32_Globalization`, `Win32_System_Diagnostics_ToolHelp` features are required. The controller entrypoint is `tests::version_history_payload::HistoryPayload_Controller_001`, ignored by the ordinary suite. Pure metadata/token rejection tests remain independent of installer execution. Rust compilation, actual restricted-token viability and installation evidence were NOT RUN during Linux authoring.
